newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Sept 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Sept 13.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- SING TAO DAILY - Senior Hong Kong civil servants failed in a court battle to overturn a government ban on them helping China to appoint a new political elite to run the territory.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST - At least 32 former senior Hong Kong government officials had joined the scramble for seats on the 400-strong Selection Committee which will choose the territory's post-handover chief executive and the provisional legislature to replace the elected chamber.

-- SING TAO DAILY - A senior Chinese official said protests in China over Japan's claim to the Diaoyu, or Senkaku islands in the East China Sea should stop, and that the dispute should be addressed through talks between the two governments.
-- HONG KONG STANDARD - Five demonstrators protesting at Japan's claim to the islands were ordered to leave Beijing.

-- ORIENTAL DAILY NEWS - A group of retired senior Chinese officials formed a group and decided to stage a protest outside the Japanese embassy in Beijing on September 18, the 65th anniversary of Japan's invasion of China.
-- Taiwanese Vice-President Lien Chan had given instructions that Taiwan would not cooperate with the mainland on the issue of the disputed islands.

-- MING PAO - Today was the 25th anniversary of the death of former Chinese People's Liberation Army leader Lin Biao, once the heir-apparent of the late chairman Mao Zedong, but who was accused of plotting to assinate Mao. Zhang Ning, who had been engaged to marry Lin's son, said Lin's image had been distorted by the Chinese leadership and that there remained many unanswered questions about his death in a plane crash.

-- MING PAO - Chinese actress Gong Li had been approached by the U.S. production house Paramount Pictures to co-star with Tom Cruise in a western production, Tai Ping Heavenly Kingdom, to be directed by Hong Kong's John Woo.
-- TA KUNG PAO - Construction of the Guangzhou-Zhuhai railway would start soon, with the project expected to be completed before the year 2000.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES - Structural changes were taking place in China's Securities and Futures Commission. Li Jiange, former secretary to Vice-Premier Zhu Rongji, would be promoted to head the commission.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST - The Bank of China will return to Hong Kong's debt market, possibly as early as next week, to issue $2 billion five-year floating rate certificates of deposit.
